v1.3.1: the continuation weights (one more pass at a lower learning rate) with one-engine serving; the Decision Index table; card suite
message: The weights are the v1.3 weights continued for one pass over the training mix at a lower learning rate, trained for both attention patterns as before (JevBench 231: 203 two-way / 198 one-way; Decision Index 0.3 public: text 57.86 / 56.72, vision 67.13 / 67.51, where two-way vision is 0.73 below v1.3, stated on the card). label_rows.lightning and serve_config.json's two-way probe anchors are recorded on these weights; adapter/ is the matching LoRA under vLLM's tensor names. serve.sh gains ONE_ENGINE=1: one generate-mode engine serving both attention modes per request and the Box question, on our vLLM build (github.com/h2oai/vllm branch h2o/per-request-attention); stock vLLM keeps the two-engine layouts. The card's measured section lists every release on the same public sets (our own runs of the public kits, not leaderboard results) and ships the card-conformance suite (test_card.py, test_card_controls.py, card_common.py). Tag v1.3.1 marks this commit; earlier tags stay.

title: card: hybrid mode answers like the merged weights (measured under identical serving settings); the earlier sentence withdrawn
message: The hybrid-mode paragraph said vLLM 0.30's LoRA path does not reproduce the merged weights exactly and that some task families differed noticeably. That rested on a comparison whose prediction file kept rows from a run with the mis-named (inactive) adapter; re-run with the renamed adapter and identical engine settings on 7,369 public-kit development questions, hybrid mode and the merged weights gave the same answer on 99.7 % of them with no measurable score difference, and 230 of 231 on the public items. Only README.md changes. Tag v1.3.0.5 marks this commit; earlier tags stay.

title: v1.3.0.4: the adapter's tensors under vLLM's names (hybrid mode served the base model since v1.3), card and packaging test
message: adapter/adapter_model.safetensors shipped since v1.3 with the key names of a text-only PEFT load (base_model.model.model.layers.N.*). vLLM 0.30 loads Qwen3.5-4B as Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration and matches LoRA tensors under base_model.model.model.language_model.layers.N.*, so none of the 496 tensors was applied and hybrid mode answered as the base model under the adapter's name, without an error (the card's adapter-active check showed identical logprobs). This commit ships the same tensors (byte-equal) under the language_model names; adapter_config.json is unchanged. The card's hybrid section says which commits were affected and what to do with an older download; test_shim.py checks every adapter key, and the new card-conformance suite (test_card.py with card_common.py and pytest.ini) runs the card's commands, examples and claims against the commit. The merged weights, the shim, serve.sh and the two-way path are untouched. Tag v1.3.0.4 marks this commit; earlier tags stay where they are.

title: v1.3.0.3: Box confidence from the generation's own token probabilities (calibrated), presence switch, guided fallback
message: The Box question's confidence is now read from the grounding generation's token logprobs and calibrated (serve_config.json box.confidence "generation", box.generation_calibration), with box.presence (the visibility yes/no readout) switchable and box.generation_temperature / box.top_logprobs / box.readout_max_pixels exposed; the calibration range is checked when the config loads; a guided decode that the engine cannot honour falls back once with a warning. box.py is the matching version (re-pinned in the shim). The card's Box section describes the fields and the measured ranking. Two-way reading, the shim's request format, serve.sh and the weights are unchanged (byte-identical to v1.3.0.2); Box itself stays off by default (LIGHTNING_BOX_ENABLED=1). Tag v1.3.0.3 marks this commit; v1.3.0.2 stays on its own.

title: serve.sh: the Box free-memory check reads the GPU in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and cannot stall or exit the script
message: With LIGHTNING_BOX_ENABLED=1 and TWO_WAY=1, serve.sh checks the GPU's free memory before starting the second (generate-mode) engine. The query now names the first GPU in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (it read the first GPU of the box whatever that variable said), is bounded by timeout 60, and an unset variable, a failed or a timed-out query take the existing WARNING branch (decisions serve two-way, a box question gets HTTP 400) instead of stalling or exiting the script. No other file changes; v1.3.0.1 stays on its commit; tag v1.3.0.2 marks this one.

title: v1.3 hotfix: the label-row file ships as label_rows.lightning (vLLM read label_rows.safetensors as a weight shard and failed to start)
message: vLLM's weight loader takes every *.safetensors file in the model folder as a shard, so the two-way label rows shipped as label_rows.safetensors beside model.safetensors stopped the engine at load ("no module or parameter named 'W'") on a plain download of main, in every serve.sh mode and the card's manual vllm serve. The file is the same bytes under label_rows.lightning (sha256 459896045499228b...), read by pooled_readout.py as before; the shim default, serve_config.json two_way.label_rows, serve.sh's check, the card and the tests follow, plus a packaging test that nothing but model.safetensors carries a weight-file suffix, and the module loader of the shim taking a lock so concurrent first Box requests never see a half-loaded module. v1.3 stays on its commit for the record (never moved); the new tag v1.3.0.1 marks this hotfix: pin it or main. A folder from the first download keeps label_rows.safetensors on a re-download: delete that file (or download into a fresh folder), then download main again; serve.sh refuses to start while it is present.

title: v1.3: dual-mode weights (two-way recommended default, one-way available), Box grounding, assets, exact label reads, wide labels
message: Decision Index 0.3 public suite (our run, official kit): text 57.10 two-way / 55.88 one-way; vision 68.00 two-way / 67.57 one-way. Weights trained to serve both attention patterns: two-way (bidirectional attention on the full-attention layers) is the recommended default since this release: serve.sh starts one vLLM 0.30.0 pooling-runner engine with the nested is_causal override and the shim reads the final hidden state with the shipped label rows (label_rows.safetensors, pooled_readout.py); one-way (causal, stock generate-mode vLLM, the earlier releases' setup) is available with TWO_WAY=0 and chosen per request with "attention_mode" when both engines run. JevBench's 231 public items on these weights: 202/231 two-way, 198/231 one-way (v1.2.3: 205/231), printed on the card with the measurement. Also in this release: Box grounding (box.py), bound assets (assets.py), every option read by its own token id (exact label reads) and the wide label set; adapter/ is the matching LoRA. Earlier tags are unchanged; a later continuation of these weights gets its own tag.

Shim: usage counts the full input and one output token per answered question
message: usage.input_tokens counts the full input: a record over max_state_tokens is cut for reading but billed as if read whole; usage.processed_input_tokens is what vLLM read. usage.output_tokens is one label token per answered question. Same on /v1/systemone and /v1/decisions. Answers are unchanged.

title: Shim: OpenAI Decisions API (POST /v1/decisions); card: example requests for both APIs
message: The shim also serves OpenAI's Decisions API (client.decisions.create in the openai Python package, 3.26 or later): input text or user messages with input_text / input_image parts, predicate / choice / score questions, mapped onto the same decision as /v1/systemone in the option format the model was trained on; the model may be named h2oai/h2o-lightning-4b or h2o-lightning-4b. The card shows tested example requests for /v1/systemone (curl and Python) and for OpenAI's client after the setup steps, and its score examples show confidence as the probability of the most likely level. /v1/systemone is unchanged.

title: Card: serving at scale (vLLM patches, flags, one-H100 numbers); serve.sh: optional VLLM_PATCHES and VLLM_ARGS
message: New section "Serving at scale": why a stock vLLM 0.30.0 runs about one multi-question decision per scheduler step on this model, two small vLLM 0.30.0 patches that fix it (shipped in vllm_patches/ with SHA256SUMS), recommended flags, one-H100 throughput and latency, and the answer effects (patches: none in our test; FP8: about 3 % of answers, near-ties, not significant). serve.sh: VLLM_PATCHES=1 applies the patches (default off, stock vLLM) and VLLM_ARGS adds vLLM flags.

title: Shim: robust backend connections; README: the base + adapter command uses the shim's image cap
message: A kept-alive connection to vLLM that the server has closed (or that sat idle) is never reused, and sending a request is bounded and retried once on a fresh connection. The manual base + adapter vllm command now sets the same image cap the shim sends (1,048,576 pixels). Answers are unchanged.

title: serve.sh: match vLLM's image cap to serve_config and warm up before ready; shim: faster image decoding
message: serve.sh now starts vLLM with the same image cap the shim sends (serve_config.json image.max_pixels) and sends a warm-up request before it reports ready, so the first request is no longer slow. The shim decodes base64 images without a per-character scan (same results, faster on large images), and a score answer's confidence is now the probability of its most likely level. The README's manual vLLM command uses the same image cap.

Shim: fetch image links safely; vLLM never fetches
message: Public https only (port 443; plain http needs LIGHTNING_IMAGE_URL_ALLOW_HTTP=true), every resolved address checked and the connection pinned to it, at most 3 redirects each re-checked, the answer must be HTTP 200 with an image/* type and real image bytes, a hard 5 s deadline and 20 MB per link, links counted before any is fetched (more than the deployment reads is refused), bytes in memory only; LIGHTNING_IMAGE_URLS=off refuses links. Adds test_security.py.
